09

“O David, are you hungry? Then We will feed you. Are you thirsty?…”

An explanation transmitted from Sufyān al-Thawrī (Q 38:24).

829
Explanation from Sufyān No. 829: 12: 7

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
829: 12:7. Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: When David, peace be upon him, came out from prostration, grass grew from his tears. He was called,
"O David, are you hungry? Then We will feed you. Are you thirsty? Then We will give you drink. Are you naked? Then We will clothe you." When he heard that his sin was not being mentioned, he began to shake violently until every limb of his seemed to leave its place. Then he was forgiven (verse 24).
العربية
829: 12: 7 سُفْيَانُ عَنْ لَيْثٍ عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ فلما خرج دَاوُدُ ﷺ سَاجِدًا نَبَتَ الْعُشْبُ مِنْ دُمُوعِهِ فَنُودِيَ يَا دَاوُدُ أَجَائِعٌ أَنْتَ فمطعمك فلا أعطشان منه أَنْتَ فَنَسْقِيَكَ أَعَارٍ أَنْتَ فَنَكْسُوَكَ فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَنَّ ذَنْبَهُ لَا يُذْكَرُ جَعَلَ يَنْتَفِضُ النَّفْضَةَ حَتَّى يَزُولَ كُلُّ عُضْوٍ مِنْهُ مِنْ مكانه فحينئذ غفر له (الآية 24) .
Edition record 371497 · p. 258Link to report ↗

“My Lord, for what did You praise Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? On…”

An explanation transmitted from Sufyān al-Thawrī (Q 38:47).

839
Explanation from Sufyān No. 839: 22: 5

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
839: 22:5. Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, from his father, who said:
Moses, peace be upon him, said, "My Lord, for what did You praise Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? On account of what did You give them that?" He said: "Abraham never set anything equal to Me without choosing Me over it. Isaac gave his own self for Me, so he is more generous with anything else. And as for Jacob, I never tried him with an affliction but it increased his good opinion of Me" (verse 47).
العربية
839: 22: 5 سفيان عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ قَالَ مُوسَى ﷺ يَا رَبِّ بِمَا أَثْنَيْتَ عَلَى ابراهيم واسحق ويعقوب بأي شئ أَعْطَيْتَهُمْ ذَلِكَ قَالَ إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لَمْ يَعْدِلْ فِيَّ شَيْئًا إِلَّا اختارني عليه وان اسحق جَادَ لِي بِنَفْسِهِ فَهُوَ بِغَيْرِهَا أَجْوَدُ وَأَمَّا يَعْقُوبُ فَلَمْ أَبْتَلِهِ بِبَلاءٍ إِلَّا زَادَ فِيَّ حُسْنَ ظن (الآية 47) .

“the highest assembly”

An explanation transmitted from Sufyān al-Thawrī (Q 38:69).

846
Explanation from Sufyān No. 846: 29: 30

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
846: 29:30. Sufyan, on His words
"the highest assembly": He said, your Lord will appear in the most beautiful form and say, "O Muhammad, what is the highest assembly disputing about?" He will say, "My Lord, I do not know." Then He will place His palm on his chest until he feels its coolness between his shoulders, and then He will not ask him about anything but he will inform Him of it (verse 69).
العربية
846: 29: 30 سفيان في قوله بالملأ الأعلى قَالَ يَتَجَلَّى رَبُّكَ فِي أَحْسَنِ صُورَةٍ فَيَقُولُ يَا مُحَمَّدُ فِيمَ يَخْتَصِمُ الْمَلأُ الْأَعْلَى فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ لَا أَدْرِي فَيَضَعُ كَفَّهُ عَلَى صَدْرِهِ حَتَّى يَجِدَ بَرْدَهَا بين كتفيه فلا يسئله عن شئ الا أخبره (الآية 69) .

23

“you are among those given respite until the day of the known time”

An explanation transmitted from Sufyān al-Thawrī (Q 38:80, 38:81).

847
Explanation from Sufyān No. 847: 30: 31

Sufyān al-Thawrī

English
Transmission wording
847: 30:31. Sufyan, on His words
"you are among those given respite until the day of the known time": He said, the first blowing of the trumpet (verses 80, 81).
العربية
847: 30: 31 سفيان في قوله إنك مِنَ الْمُنْظَرِينَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْوَقْتِ المعلوم قال النفخة الأولى (الآية 80، 81) .
